purpose: Authoritative-vendor evidence delta adding Parsable Connected Worker and Dozuki at spec-verified only. Adds a reusable versioned HTTP RPC/JSON profile for read-via-POST APIs, reuses the existing REST profile for Dozuki, records WFM data/value/security boundaries, and does not enable writes or claim sandbox/tenant evidence.

systems.name: Parsable Connected Worker
systems.evidenceNote: Parsable's official API documentation identifies API version 1.24.102 and an HTTPS JSON RPC-style contract in which calls are POSTed to module endpoints, method/arguments are carried in JSON, and a Wi-Thrift-Version header selects the target API version. Authentication uses JWT-encoded tokens; persistent tokens are associated with a system user on a team and are intended for automated systems. Documented modules include jobs, job templates, field data, reporting, analytics, teams, users, notifications and reference sheets. The API's use of POST for reads must not be mistaken for write authority: WFM therefore adds a dedicated read-via-POST protocol profile and keeps mutation methods disabled. No Parsable tenant or credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Parsable system user with the minimum team role and data visibility needed for approved read methods
vendor-issued persistent token for that constrained system user; do not reuse a human user's normal token for unattended production integration
API access limited to approved read/reporting/analytics/job/user/team modules and methods; mutation methods remain blocked
pin the supported Wi-Thrift-Version/API version and re-verify before version changes
dataAvailableOrExpected: users and team membership visible to the integration identity
jobs, job templates, job roles and job-filter context
field/work-execution data captured by frontline procedures
reporting and analytics outputs exposed by the customer's Parsable configuration
notifications, metadata and reference-sheet data where required for approved WFM use cases
automationOpportunities: use frontline job/execution evidence to compare planned labour with actual work completion and identify delay or rework patterns
feed approved user/team structures into implementation mapping to reduce duplicate workforce administration
correlate work-execution and issue data with staffing, overtime and skills mix for labour-productivity improvement
surface maintenance, quality or operational exceptions into WFM manager decision support without allowing the read connector to mutate Parsable
after separate write certification, consider narrowly approved work-assignment or workflow hand-offs using explicitly classified mutation methods
savingsHypotheses: reduce supervisor administration by reusing job, user, team and execution data already captured on the frontline
reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by comparing staffing with actual job completion and interruption evidence
reduce rework and repeat delays by identifying procedures and staffing patterns associated with poor execution outcomes
improve labour-cost attribution by joining frontline execution events to WFM time and payroll evidence
dataGaps: public documentation does not establish the customer's exact team-role permissions or a universal read-only role for every module
authoritative employment contracts, payroll, absence, agency-worker and broad qualification data normally remain outside Parsable
the exact semantics of customer-created jobs, field data and reference sheets are tenant specific and require customer mappings
public documentation reviewed does not establish a universal rate-limit contract across all modules
site, line, asset and worker identifiers require deterministic reconciliation with HCM, MES, CMMS and WFM masters
constraintsRisks: Parsable reads use HTTP POST, so generic verb-based write blocking would be incorrect; safety must classify the RPC method, not the HTTP verb
the Wi-Thrift-Version header is contract-significant and API version drift can change request/response types
persistent tokens are tied to a system user/team and effective permissions must be tenant-tested before promotion
analytics/reporting exports can expose broader data than a frontline workflow and remain subject to cross-scope and data-minimisation gates
retrying a POST-carried read must be limited to methods proven side-effect-free; unknown methods fail closed
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the new HTTP RPC/JSON adapter profile. In an authorised Parsable tenant, provision a dedicated least-privilege system user and persistent token, enumerate permitted modules/methods, prove which methods are side-effect-free reads, pin the supported Wi-Thrift-Version, test pagination/version errors/retries/rate limits and representative user/team/job/reporting reads, fingerprint tenant-specific field schemas, reconcile worker/site/work-centre identities, and normalise representative records before promotion beyond spec verification.

systems.name: Dozuki
systems.evidenceNote: Dozuki's official API v2.0 documentation identifies v2.0 as the current version, uses JSON over standard HTTP verbs, documents token authentication, limit/offset pagination, users/teams/guides/categories, course assignments/completions and work-log records. Persistent API tokens are available for automated access. The API also exposes create/update/delete operations, so WFM reuses only the existing REST read path and keeps all mutation authority disabled. Public or unauthenticated content endpoints do not count as tenant evidence. No Dozuki tenant or credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated persistent API token associated with a customer-approved integration identity where unattended access is required
GET/read access limited to approved users, teams, guides, courses, course-assignee/completion and work-log resources
no guide/course/user mutation, assignment changes or content administration in the normal WFM read connector
private-site authentication must be proven; publicly reachable content must not be treated as authenticated customer data
dataAvailableOrExpected: registered users and employment-related fields returned by approved user endpoints
guides, categories and standard-work/procedure content metadata
courses, course assignees, due dates, stage progress and completion history
work-log entries including guide, user and customer work-order identifiers plus timing/work data
revision/version identifiers and content history needed to detect changed procedures
automationOpportunities: enrich scheduling readiness with approved course/training completion evidence while keeping qualification policy authoritative
identify overdue or incomplete training before assigning work that depends on the customer's training policy
reuse user/team structures and standard-work metadata during implementation to reduce duplicate configuration
join work-log timing and work-order evidence to WFM time/cost data for labour-standard and productivity analysis
detect changed guide revisions so workers can be retrained or alerted when standard work materially changes
after separate write certification, consider tightly controlled course assignment or workflow hand-offs without granting content administration authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce manual training checks by reusing course assignment, progress and completion history in workforce planning
reduce avoidable assignment errors by flagging missing required training before a shift or task is allocated
reduce implementation and master-data effort by reusing Dozuki user/team/work-order references instead of recreating them manually
improve labour standards and cost attribution by comparing Dozuki work-log duration with WFM paid time and production outcomes
dataGaps: course completion is training evidence and must not automatically become a qualification or legal work-eligibility decision
authoritative payroll, contracts, absence, agency labour and most shift availability remain outside Dozuki
public documentation does not establish a universal least-privilege token scope or rate-limit contract for every customer plan
work-order, team and user identifiers require reconciliation with ERP/MES/HCM/WFM masters
customer-specific guide fields, course structures and employment fields can vary and require schema/mapping discovery
constraintsRisks: Dozuki supports public sites and some unauthenticated reads; those surfaces are useful for documentation verification but cannot satisfy tenant-authenticated evidence
the same API family exposes POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE operations, so WFM must allowlist GET/read endpoints and keep mutation disabled
API v2.0 is current but the vendor states older versions can be removed; version pinning and upgrade checks are required
pagination uses both limit/offset and newer course-specific page/pageSize patterns, so adapters must support endpoint-specific pagination
guide revisions and course history are temporal evidence; downstream mappings must preserve source version/event time rather than overwrite history
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST adapter. In an authorised Dozuki tenant, obtain a dedicated persistent token, enumerate effective read permissions, prove private-site authentication, exercise users/teams/courses/course-completion/work-log GET endpoints with both pagination styles, record rate-limit/error behaviour, fingerprint customer guide/course schemas and revisions, reconcile workers/teams/work orders to canonical WFM identities, and normalise representative records before promotion beyond spec verification.
